scope.population: 2,480,267 collapsed taker fills, row-aligned across the two intermediates ({'coin': True, 'day': True, 'taker_side': True, 'notional': True}); no wallet floor is applied and no counterparty identity field is read at all. pi is estimated over 50 equal-count buckets per (coin, day), each needing at least 5 fills
scope.window: 10 days present in the input, day-of-month 4..13; early [4, 5, 6, 7, 8], late [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

override_reasons.horizon_s: this file is stamped at 60s because J -- the SIZE of the informed jump, read as mean|a_mid| -- needs the window by which the permanent revision has finished. That is a magnitude, not a ranking, so it is not the 10s scoring window and is_headline_horizon is correctly false here
override_reasons.master_seed: the streams here are seeded 20260623, not the declared 20260620; settings.MASTER_SEED carries the state 'target', so adopting it is a measured change owed its own recompute
override_reasons.n_perm: no permutation test and no bootstrap run in this file, so neither declared resampling budget applies
override_reasons.rank_floor_fills: no wallet floor applies: this quoter reads no counterparty identity at all, so it never ranks or gates a per-wallet population

_meta.object: Glosten-Milgrom (1985) information-based market-level-toxicity counterparty-blind maker (one quoter in the bake-off)
_meta.author: Dmitry Stakhin
_meta.split_rule: The early and late halves are DERIVED from the days present, by settings.split_early_late: first ceil(n/2) days early, the rest late. They used to be the hardcoded day-of-month tuples (4,5,6,7,8) and (9,10,11,12,13), which are correct only for a window opening on the 4th and closing on the 13th. This input does open on the 4th, so the derived split reproduces those tuples exactly and no number moved.

closed_form.half_spread: half_spread = pi * J  (pi = P(informed), J = E[|adverse move|])
closed_form.quotes: bid = mid - pi*J ; ask = mid + pi*J ; total = 2*pi*J
closed_form.pi_estimator: VPIN/PIN proxy: mean over equal-count buckets of |sum(sign_taker)|/n per (coin, day); MARKET-LEVEL, no identity

_meta.units: pi dimensionless in [0,1); J in price units (or bps); half_spread = pi*J in the same units; bps form directly comparable to spread_entry_bps/2.
_meta.sign_convention: taker_side 1=buy-aggressor(+1)/0=sell-aggressor(-1); positive a_mid markout = adverse for the passive maker; pi=0 => half_spread=0; half_spread widens in pi and J.
_meta.counterfactual_only: markout-based counterfactual overlay, NOT a matching engine (no queue / fill-probability / requote); the only fill-awareness is the maker_econ-style recapture APPROXIMATION (fraction f at +h bps minus penalty c).
_meta.cost_not_alpha: every quoter is expected net-NEGATIVE at every maker-fee tier; GM is never framed as profitable/alpha/edge/Sharpe; GM cannot reach the counterparty term's (whale-driven, fragile, ETH-tilted) cost reduction.
_meta.lineage: the adverse-selection-aware quoting leg is owned by Barzykin-Bergault-Gueant-Lemmel (arXiv:2508.20225); GM (1985) is the founding information-based spread the lineage descends from, used here as the book-only baseline, not as new quoting theory.
_meta.no_repull: computed entirely on-disk from the two npz; no S3 re-pull.

pi_estimation_vpin_pin.method: VPIN/PIN proxy: per (coin, day), equal-COUNT bucket fills in arrival order into N_VPIN_BUCKETS buckets, pi = mean over buckets of |sum(sign)|/n (absolute buy/sell imbalance). MARKET-LEVEL toxicity only -- NO counterparty identity. Count clock substitutes for the volume clock (notional heavy-tailed). No lookahead: each (coin, day) pi uses that day's fills only.

adverse_move_J.method: J = E[|adverse move|] read off the EXEC->mid book-mid markout a_mid_{h}: per coin, J_bps = mean(|a_mid_{h}|) (positive a_mid is adverse for the maker; |.| is the GM jump magnitude regardless of direction). MARKET-LEVEL, NOT counterparty-conditioned. J_price = J_bps/1e4 * mid.

gm_spread_vs_real.formula: gm_half_spread_bps = pi * J_bps ; gm_total_spread_bps = 2 * pi * J_bps
gm_spread_vs_real.interpretation: GM prices the ADVERSE-SELECTION share of the spread only (no inventory, no processing cost), from MARKET-LEVEL toxicity (pi) and the average informed move (J). It is the book-only-information baseline; it cannot price WHO the counterparty is, which is the gap the counterparty-resolved term fills. No profit/alpha claim.

gm_net_economics.label: GM net-economics counterfactual on the LATE half. net_MID_GM = h_GM - a_mid (GM model half-spread as income minus realized book-mid markout); net_PRINT = -a_print (maker_econ measure 1). COUNTERFACTUAL, not a fill model. Every tier expected net-NEGATIVE = COST, never alpha.

recapture_approx.note: maker_econ-style fill-aware APPROXIMATION (recapture fraction f of would-be fills at the wider GM quote minus a per-requote penalty); labelled an approximation, NOT a matching-engine fill model.

bakeoff_mapping_note.role: GM is the INFORMATION-based, book-only-toxicity quoter in the bake-off, between the inventory-only Avellaneda-Stoikov maker (as_quoter.py) and the counterparty-toxicity-conditioned skew overlay (t1_*/maker_econ.py). GM prices the adverse-selection share of the spread from MARKET-LEVEL flow toxicity (a VPIN/PIN proxy) and the average informed move, with NO counterparty identity.
bakeoff_mapping_note.hard_limit: GM quotes ONE spread to every counterparty given the market-level pi; it cannot reach the per-counterparty idiosyncratic adverse selection the wallet-resolved term reaches, BY CONSTRUCTION -- that is the point of the bake-off. The idiosyncratic component is not recoverable from the pooled book-only signal GM uses.
bakeoff_mapping_note.expected_ranking: On adverse-selection-cost reduction the expected ordering is: symmetric A-S (no AS term) <= GM (market-level AS term) <= counterparty-resolved overlay (market + idiosyncratic AS). GM is expected to IMPROVE on symmetric A-S by pricing average toxicity, yet fall SHORT of the counterparty term because it is blind to who trades. All three are expected net-NEGATIVE at every maker-fee tier (COST, not alpha); GM vs A-S may be a near-tie when the market-level toxicity signal is weak, which is itself a reportable finding.
bakeoff_mapping_note.what_gm_is_not: GM produces a spread, never an alpha, a P&L, or a Sharpe. It is a baseline quoter, and the counterparty-resolved term is measured against it as well as against A-S.
